Drama New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Drama, Greece

Not demolished. Benjamin of Tudela documented 140 Jews in Drama in the 12th century; a small community persisted through the 17th century, reaching 150 by the late 19th and 600 by 1912. A new Jewish school replaced an older one in 1925, alongside various welfare and Zionist organizations. Following Bulgarian occupation in spring 1941, population reached 1,200; on March 4, 1943, all Jews were arrested and transferred to a Bulgarian transit camp, then handed to German forces, shipped, and eventually deported via Vienna to Treblinka - of 780 Jews, only a few survived. This newer of Drama's two cemeteries has an unknown founding date, presumed either the 17th or 19th century.
